export const meta = {
  name: 'globe-design',
  description: 'Rendering and pipeline analyses, then three competing architectures judged by three lenses and synthesised',
  phases: [
    { title: 'Analyse and design', detail: 'W11 rendering, W12 pipeline, three designers' },
    { title: 'Judge', detail: 'three judges score all three designs' },
    { title: 'Synthesise', detail: 'one design section from the winner plus grafts' },
  ],
}

const REPO = '/home/user/RoofingApp'
const EVID = REPO + '/research/globe/validation-evidence/'
const SCRATCH = '/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-RoofingApp/7638440a-a008-5ef8-a289-86be0a23e7a7/scratchpad'

const CTX = `You are one of several agents working on the "globe view" research scaffold for RoofingApp, a Montana roofing company's weather desktop app. A supervisor reads your output; it is data, not prose for a person.

Read first, in this order:
1. ${REPO}/research/globe/README.md sections 1-7 (the plan, written before the evidence; several of its numbers were corrected by the evidence).
2. ${SCRATCH}/supervisor-log.md — the supervisor's verdicts on two critiques of the plan (the "ACCEPT" list is binding for you; the "REJECT" list explains what the supervisor kept and why) and the wave-1 refuter verdicts.
3. The evidence files under ${EVID} that your task names. Where a file has a "review" key, the review's corrections win over its "facts". Where a file has no "review" key yet, treat its facts as unreviewed: re-check live any fact you build a conclusion on (a size, a version, a licence sentence) and say you did.
4. ${REPO}/AGENTS.md hard rules and ${REPO}/docs/DECISIONS.md (D1, D2, D4, D7-D9, D12, D19, D23, D24), ${REPO}/docs/ROADMAP.md.

Binding constraints: Python first (rule 4 / D1: all data, time, geometry, thresholds and freshness logic in Python; browser JavaScript only draws and handles browser-only events, each duty documented); the self-test runs with the network off and checks HTTP status only; the 50 MiB cap is the WHOLE-REPO zipball; a new pip package means a new installer (rule 2); evidence kinds and freshness limits change only by a DECISIONS entry; no "best" claims (rule 9); evidence honesty (rule 5): observation / satellite estimate / radar estimate / official alert never merged, never damage, no echo is not clear, MRMS -99 and -999 are "no radar data" (meanings unverified), MRMS levels are heights above mean sea level (the 0.5 km level is below ground over most of Montana), cloud-top height is an estimate of the top only, parallax wording from ${EVID}parallax.json; no paid token in browser code; no saved-place lists sent to any third-party job (publish fixed statewide products); the 3D view ships behind a default-off setting.

Working rules: today is 2026-10-17 (UTC); outbound HTTPS works; use WebFetch/WebSearch (ToolSearch "select:WebFetch,WebSearch") for pages and quote the sentence you rely on with its URL. Write ONLY the one output file your task names (JSON, at most 30 KB) under ${EVID}. Never write model names or AI-vendor identifiers into any file. Do not modify any other repo file. Numbers carry units and a source (an evidence file name, a URL, or "computed: <formula>"); anything else is marked unverified.`

const ANALYSIS_SCHEMA = {
  type: 'object',
  properties: {
    slug: { type: 'string' },
    output_file: { type: 'string' },
    headline: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } },
    numbers: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } },
    unverified: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } },
    questions_for_owner: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } },
  },
  required: ['slug', 'output_file', 'headline', 'numbers', 'unverified'],
}

const DESIGN_SCHEMA = {
  type: 'object',
  properties: {
    slug: { type: 'string' },
    output_file: { type: 'string' },
    name: { type: 'string' },
    one_paragraph: { type: 'string' },
    js_duties: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } },
    pip_packages_added: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } },
    offline_and_selftest_behaviour: { type: 'string' },
    phases: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } },
    biggest_risks: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } },
  },
  required: ['slug', 'output_file', 'name', 'one_paragraph', 'js_duties', 'pip_packages_added', 'offline_and_selftest_behaviour', 'phases', 'biggest_risks'],
}

const JUDGE_SCHEMA = {
  type: 'object',
  properties: {
    lens: { type: 'string' },
    output_file: { type: 'string' },
    scores: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'object', properties: { design: { type: 'string' }, score_0_to_10: { type: 'number' }, reasons: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } }, fatal_flaws: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } } }, required: ['design', 'score_0_to_10', 'reasons', 'fatal_flaws'] } },
    ranking: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } },
    grafts: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } },
    facts_rechecked: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } },
  },
  required: ['lens', 'output_file', 'scores', 'ranking', 'grafts', 'facts_rechecked'],
}

const W11 = `# Task W11 — rendering techniques for clouds and storms on a globe (slug: rendering)
Read ${EVID}mrms.json, goes-aws.json, gibs.json, globe-libs.json, webgl-runtime.json, parallax.json, and if present prototype-mrms.json and prototype-globe.json (measured voxel counts, bytes and draw results from the prototype).
Produce ${EVID}rendering-options.json: for each technique — (a) draped satellite texture, (b) cloud deck displaced by cloud-top height (mesh vertex displacement), (c) volumetric ray-marching in a 3D texture (WebGL2 Data3DTexture / custom shader), (d) sparse voxel points or boxes from MRMS (what the prototype draws), (e) isosurfaces (marching cubes in Python → glTF / 3D Tiles) at 20/35/50 dBZ display classes, (f) stacked translucent slabs per level, (g) 2D fallback drape (NWS WMS) — give: data needed; where computed (Python server-side vs browser); bytes to the browser per frame for the Montana + border box at the measured voxel counts (computed from the evidence numbers, formula shown); GPU and memory load class (low/medium/high with the reason: counts of points, texture sizes versus MAX_3D_TEXTURE_SIZE 2048 from webgl-runtime.json); what it honestly represents and the legend text it needs; failure modes (sub-terrain MSL levels; parallax; no-data cells; frame gaps; interpolation creating false precision — forbidden); which library supports it (from globe-libs.json, re-check the API doc for any claim you rely on); which phase it fits. Rank per phase with reasons; no "best". Also survey, with URLs and quoted sentences, 3-5 existing viewers that draw GOES or radar in 3D or pseudo-3D (open-source or public) and what technique each uses.`

const W12 = `# Task W12 — data pipeline and cost (slug: pipeline)
Read ${EVID}mrms.json, goes-aws.json, hosting-options.json, app-integration.json, webgl-runtime.json, and if present prototype-mrms.json and prototype-goes.json (measured download bytes, decode times, output bytes).
Produce ${EVID}pipeline-options.json comparing: (A) on each crew machine: download + decode on the desktop (needs eccodes + netCDF4 in the installer under rule 2 — measure the wheel sizes with "pip download --no-deps" for eccodes, eccodeslib, netCDF4, numpy into a scratch directory and report bytes; bytes per hour per machine from the evidence; CPU time from prototype measurements); (B) a scheduled job on GitHub Actions (5-min minimum, drops, terms doubt — from hosting-options.json) publishing fixed statewide products to object storage; (C) a small always-on server (prices in hosting-options.json; roadmap item 8 already needs one) producing the same products; (D) hybrid: server publishes products, desktop crops locally. For each: bytes per 2-min MRMS step and per 5-min GOES step in and out (formulas shown), monthly transfer per crew machine for a 12-hour storm day season, $/month from the quoted prices, latency added, failure surfacing and staleness fields, privacy (no place lists leave the machine), installer impact, what the self-test must do. Define the frame-bytes budget the plan's Phase 3 cites: a number per frame and per 2-hour loop with its derivation from the measured voxel counts at thresholds 20 and 35 dBZ. State the product format you propose (compact JSON vs binary + sidecar) with sizes. Include the MESH footprint job of roadmap item 4 as the same job. Rank with reasons; no "best".`

const DESIGNERS = [
  { slug: 'design-a', name: 'A — Jinja-generated CesiumJS page inside the Flask app (/globe)', brief: `Design the globe as a page of the existing payload: a Flask route /globe rendering a Jinja template that embeds configuration and layer lists computed in Python (the way Folium generates Leaflet today — note the app already loads Leaflet from a CDN, see supervisor-log.md), loads CesiumJS from a pinned CDN with an integrity hash, and a small documented JavaScript file that only draws. Data endpoints under /api/globe/… computed by Python (alerts with zone geometry handling, layer states, volume and cloud-height products). Behind a default-off setting. Must pass the self-test offline. Use the prototype under ${REPO}/research/globe/prototype as evidence of what works (read serve.py and globe.js, and prototype-globe.json if present).` },
  { slug: 'design-b', name: 'B — separate globe window served by the desktop shell, outside the payload', brief: `Design the globe as a second local server/window started by the desktop shell (desktop/launcher.py pattern: private port, session key, Host check), kept out of the self-updating payload so the globe library and any heavy decoders can ship with a new installer rather than through the 50 MiB zipball; the payload only links to it and shares the SQLite database read-only. Consider what this costs in installer churn (D3: desktop changes only with a new installer) and how updates reach crews. Use the prototype under ${REPO}/research/globe/prototype as evidence.` },
  { slug: 'design-c', name: 'C — Python-first 2.5D without a globe library, or a Python-wrapped globe (pydeck)', brief: `Design the most Python-first option that still meets the owner's wish for 3D clouds and storms: either (i) pydeck / deck.gl GlobeView generated from Python (check globe-libs.json and re-check pydeck's GlobeView support live — quote), with its installer impact under rule 2; or (ii) staying on the Folium flat map with 2.5D encodings computed in Python (radar echo tops as colour, cloud-top height contours, a side elevation profile image rendered server-side), i.e. no globe library at all. State plainly what each sub-option cannot do that the owner asked for, and what it protects (rule 4, D1, offline self-test, no CDN). Use the prototype under ${REPO}/research/globe/prototype only as a comparison.` },
]

function designPrompt(d) {
  return CTX + `\n\n# Task W13 — architecture design ${d.name} (slug: ${d.slug})\n${d.brief}\nRead ${EVID}globe-libs.json, webgl-runtime.json, app-integration.json, hosting-options.json, mrms.json, goes-aws.json, gibs.json, parallax.json, and ${REPO}/payload/app.py, payload/maps.py, payload/templates/live.html, desktop/launcher.py, desktop/updater.py (read-only).\nProduce ${EVID}${d.slug}.json with: name; summary; components (each with language, where it runs, what it owns); the COMPLETE list of hand-written JavaScript duties with a one-line reason each must run in the browser (this list is what the owner rules on); pip packages added (none, or which, and the installer consequence); library pin and integrity policy; offline and self-test behaviour (state per layer: "off" in the self-test; stale/unavailable live; "3D view could not load" separate from data states); data endpoints and their Python owners (reuse of weather.py functions by name from app-integration.json); evidence-kind and freshness entries needed (as DECISIONS proposals); alert handling for null geometry (zone outline, marker + text, can't-tell); how the 3D storms layer handles MSL levels below terrain, no-data codes, legend text and no interpolation; the default-off setting; route security tests; phases with numeric done-when checks and a stop option each; size impact on the zipball (numbers); risks ranked; what the owner must decide. No "best" claims; cite evidence files for every number.`
}

function judgePrompt(lens, designs) {
  return CTX + `\n\n# Task W13 — judge the three designs through the lens: ${lens.name} (slug: judge-${lens.slug})\nThe designs are ${EVID}design-a.json, ${EVID}design-b.json, ${EVID}design-c.json (summaries: ${JSON.stringify(designs.map(d => d && { slug: d.slug, name: d.name, one_paragraph: d.one_paragraph, js_duties: d.js_duties, pip_packages_added: d.pip_packages_added }))}).\n${lens.criteria}\nScore each design 0-10 on this lens only, with reasons that cite evidence files, repo rules (file:line) or facts you re-checked live; list fatal flaws (a rule or decision the design cannot satisfy without an owner decision — name the decision); rank; and list grafts (specific ideas from losing designs the winner should adopt). Re-check at least three facts the designs rely on against the evidence files' review keys or live requests, and list them. Write ${EVID}judge-${lens.slug}.json.`
}

const LENSES = [
  { slug: 'rules', name: 'rules and evidence honesty', criteria: 'Criteria: compliance with AGENTS.md hard rules 1-9 and DECISIONS D1-D4, D12, D19, D23; how little JavaScript carries logic; evidence kinds and freshness handled by DECISIONS entries; null-geometry alerts; no-data and sub-terrain handling; legends; demo policy; no paid tokens in the browser; privacy of place lists; the default-off setting; route security.' },
  { slug: 'engineering', name: 'engineering cost and risk', criteria: 'Criteria: installer and SHELL_API impact (rule 2, D3); zipball size (whole-repo 50 MiB cap, numbers); offline self-test behaviour; WebGL availability on WebView2 / WKWebView / Linux (webgl-runtime.json); CDN dependence and integrity; update path to crews (D3-D6); maintenance burden (lines of JavaScript, number of moving parts, test surface); performance plausibility from the prototype measurements; failure modes and how they surface.' },
  { slug: 'product', name: 'value to the office and crews, and fit with the pilot', criteria: 'Criteria: which decisions the view improves for which person (read ${SCRATCH}/plan-critique-product.json jobs_to_be_done); honesty traps avoided; fit with the roadmap order (installers, pilot, baseline — ROADMAP items 1-3 and the "baseline before any new feed" line) and with keeping the crews\' screen unchanged during the pilot; demo value with DEMO-only data; mobile/field reachability (open question); what the owner literally asked for (a Google Earth-like globe with 3D clouds and storms) versus what each design delivers.' },
]

const SYNTH = (judges, designs) => CTX + `\n\n# Task W13 — synthesise the design section (slug: design-synthesis)\nThree designers (${EVID}design-a.json, design-b.json, design-c.json) and three judges (${EVID}judge-rules.json, judge-engineering.json, judge-product.json) have reported. Judge summaries: ${JSON.stringify(judges.map(j => j && { lens: j.lens, ranking: j.ranking, grafts: j.grafts }))}.\nWrite ${EVID}design-synthesis.json: the recommended architecture (one of A/B/C or a named hybrid), why (citing the judges' scores and the evidence), the grafts adopted from the others, the complete JavaScript duty list for the owner's ruling, the pip/installer consequence, the DECISIONS entries it needs (proposed wording for each: evidence kinds, freshness limits, library pin and integrity policy, publish host, the Folium-CDN correction to D23), the phase plan with numeric done-when and stop criteria, the owner decisions it depends on (map them to D-G1…D-G9 from the README and add any new ones), and the dissent (what the losing designs do better and when the owner should prefer them). Keep it under 30 KB; no "best" claims; every number cites an evidence file.`

log('Wave 2b: rendering + pipeline analyses and three designers in parallel')
const [w11, w12, dA, dB, dC] = await parallel([
  () => agent(CTX + '\n\n' + W11, { label: 'analyse:rendering', phase: 'Analyse and design', model: 'haiku', schema: ANALYSIS_SCHEMA }),
  () => agent(CTX + '\n\n' + W12, { label: 'analyse:pipeline', phase: 'Analyse and design', model: 'haiku', schema: ANALYSIS_SCHEMA }),
  () => agent(designPrompt(DESIGNERS[0]), { label: 'design:A', phase: 'Analyse and design', model: 'haiku', schema: DESIGN_SCHEMA }),
  () => agent(designPrompt(DESIGNERS[1]), { label: 'design:B', phase: 'Analyse and design', model: 'haiku', schema: DESIGN_SCHEMA }),
  () => agent(designPrompt(DESIGNERS[2]), { label: 'design:C', phase: 'Analyse and design', model: 'haiku', schema: DESIGN_SCHEMA }),
])
const designs = [dA, dB, dC]
log('Wave 2b: three judges scoring all designs')
const judges = await parallel(LENSES.map(l => () => agent(judgePrompt(l, designs), { label: 'judge:' + l.slug, phase: 'Judge', model: 'haiku', schema: JUDGE_SCHEMA })))
log('Wave 2b: synthesis')
const synthesis = await agent(SYNTH(judges, designs), { label: 'synthesis', phase: 'Synthesise', model: 'haiku', schema: ANALYSIS_SCHEMA })
return { w11, w12, designs, judges, synthesis }

headline: Phase 1: draped GOES imagery (a) first, NWS radar drape (g) as fallback; both low GPU load.

Phase 2: cloud deck lifted by cloud-top height (b). 2 km ACHA2KMC ranks first on footprint (4.9 x 2.2 km vs 24 x 11 km), gated on a DQF-0 count not yet measured; 10 km ACHAC ranks second on server bytes.

Phase 3: sparse boxes (d) at 50 then 35 dBZ first; isosurfaces (e) after d with an interpolation caveat; ray-marching (c) only as a measured experiment (27.4 MB dense texture per frame); stacked slabs (f) as level inspector only.

Honesty rules that bind all options: no interpolation between levels or grid cells; MRMS levels are above sea level and 0.5/0.75 km sit below ground at Billings; no-data is not clear; uncorrected parallax is disclosed; ACHA height is geopotential (about sea level), not ground.

No browser-based GOES or NEXRAD 3D volume viewer found in nine searches. Survey: Blue Raster (ArcGIS Pro voxels), Nexrad Spatial VR (ray-marched voxels, Unreal Engine 5.7), Purdue/TeraGrid (GPU texture volume renderer with VNC), Windy (flat maps on a globe; negative control).
No GPU timing exists: every WebGL number is SwiftShader in headless Chromium 141; GPU classes are reasoned from counts and sizes.
numbers: Voxel JSON per frame, 2025-06-15 23:12:41Z event peak, 33 levels, Montana+border box (1350 x 615 per level): >=20 dBZ 619,321 voxels = 10.33 MB; >=35 dBZ 99,854 = 1.67 MB; >=50 dBZ 13,482 = 0.23 MB (prototype-mrms.json, out-v2 files). Quiet frame 2026-10-17T03:04:41Z: 0 voxels, 9,642 B.
Dense 3D texture per frame: 1350 x 615 x 33 = 27,398,250 texels = 27.40 MB uint8 / 54.80 MB uint16; 822 MB per hour uint8 (computed). Whole-CONUS 33-level gz step 20.0 MB (mrms.json, measured).

Ray-march fetches: 900 x 720 x 33 = 21.4 M per frame = 1.28 G per second at 60 fps (computed). MAX_3D_TEXTURE_SIZE 2048 (webgl-runtime.json, SwiftShader) fits the plan box (1350, 615, 33) but not CONUS 7000 x 3500.

Isosurface proxy from exposed voxel faces x 2 triangles x 72 B (computed; non-indexed): 20 / 35 / 50 dBZ = 51.7 / 11.5 / 2.16 MB per frame = 5.0x / 6.9x / 9.3x the voxel JSON (prototype-mrms.json out-v2 voxel sets).
GIBS Montana 2 x 2 box: 0.28-0.42 MB per layer per 10-min frame (gibs.json, measured). Python-made C13 PNG at 0.02 deg, plan box: 128.8 KB per 5-min frame (prototype-goes.json, unreviewed).

ACHAC 10 km, Montana review box: 1,777 cells, 733 valid (41.2%), 01:41 (goes-aws.json). 2 km grid, same box: 44,363 cells (goes-aws.json). Native height bytes per frame: 3.6 KB at 10 km, 88.7 KB at 2 km (computed, 2 B per cell).
Pixel footprint at the Montana box centre (GOES-East): 10 km 24.4 x 10.9 km; 2 km 4.9 x 2.2 km (prototype-goes.json, unreviewed).

Parallax (parallax.json, geometry): uncorrected cloud tops 3-4 km off for a 2 km top, 20-33 km off for 12-15 km (34 km if GOES-East origin -75.0 is used, not -75.2; live re-read of kept NOAA object; shift change up to 0.171 km at 15 km).
Per-cell linear displacement model calibrated at 12 km reproduces parallax.json rows at 2-15 km within 0.042 km (computed from table, 4 sites x 2 satellites).
Billings elevation 952 m (terrain.json): MRMS 0.5 km and 0.75 km levels below ground; 1.0 km level 48 m above ground.
Coverage of valid height (DQF 0) at 03:28 UTC scene, plan box: GOES-East 1,270 of 2,647 native 10 km cells (48.0%); GOES-West 1,535 of 3,042 (50.5%) (prototype-goes.json, unreviewed).
Per 2-hour loop upper bounds at peak sample (60 MRMS frames): d 50 dBZ 14 MB; d 35 dBZ 100 MB; d 20 dBZ 620 MB; c dense uint8 1,644 MB; e 50 dBZ 130 MB (proxy).
unverified: Meanings of MRMS -99 and -999 (NSSL table unreadable); MESH units and codes -1 and -3.
ACHA2KMC DQF-0 share in the Montana box (not measured; 2 km 13,125 cells at 00:01 include unknown DQF split).
Mesh and isosurface sizes are face-count proxies from voxel faces; no mesher was run; gzip or Brotli sizes not measured.
All GPU timings and memory (SwiftShader only); crew laptop GPU class unknown; 2048 cap is SwiftShader, not a real GPU.

Plan-box GOES numbers (native counts, 17.2 and 20.1 KB PNGs, footprints, DQF shares) come from prototype-goes.json, which has no review key; not re-run except the -75.0 origin and HT standard name, re-read from the kept NOAA object.
Echo-bearing NWS WMS export size and cadence (only a blank 866 B export is reported, URL not recorded).
Montana-wide share of MRMS levels below ground (only Billings checked).
Geoid-to-ellipsoid offset for ACHA height not applied or quantified; parallax table assumes ellipsoid heights.
Purdue paper date; Windy post date (deleted notice); Nexrad Spatial VR licence name.
Cesium WMTS time-dimension and CustomShader scope rest on wave-1 raw HTML, not re-fetched; no marching-cubes or glTF tool was checked.
questions_for_owner: Phase 2 product: ACHA2KMC (2 km; 4.4-4.5 MB per 5-min server file) or ACHAC (10 km; 0.32 MB per file)? The 2 km ranking needs a DQF-0 count for the Montana box first.
Phase 3 classes: 50 and 35 dBZ first (proposed), or 20 dBZ too (10.3 MB per peak frame before a budget exists)?
If the GOES-East origin of -75.0 is confirmed, the parallax.json legend wording needs a recheck (upper bound about 34 km rather than 33 km).

headline: Ranking by open blockers today, not by merit: D, then C, then B, then A. The ranking is not a 'best' claim and all four stay open until the host decision (D-G2) is made.

D (server decodes once and publishes one statewide >=20 dBZ product per 2-min step; the desktop derives 35/50 dBZ and crops to saved places): 0.732 MB per active frame; 0.07 / 2.28 GB per machine-month (quiet / all frames active) at 8.5 storm days and a 30-day month; host floor $6.49/mo with RAM unverified; server 24/7 ingest about 498 GB/month is not priced.
C (same products as B, always-on server, one file per threshold): 1.56x D's active bytes because the three files repeat the mask; same host and blockers as D.

B (scheduled GitHub Actions job to object storage): 5-min floor cannot publish every 2-min step; drops are silent; the Actions terms clause 'don't use Actions as a content delivery network' needs an owner or legal reading. R2 costs $0 at this volume.

A (each crew machine downloads NOAA GRIB2 and decodes): 70.5 GB per machine-month at 33 levels; about 15% of one core per 2-min frame; eccodes has no Windows wheel on pip, so Windows is blocked until a native source is chosen.

Frame budget proposed for README section 10 (the section does not exist yet): 1.0 MB per 2-min MRMS frame (measured peak keyframe 0.836 MB; 0.965 B per >=20 dBZ voxel x 619,321 voxels + 0.238 MB mask); 60 MB per 2-h loop at >=20 dBZ (measured worst 44.5 MB); 20 MB per loop for the 35 dBZ shell (estimate 15.8 MB from 99,854 voxels); 0.05 MB per GOES 5-min frame (measured 0.032 MB).

Product format: binary payload plus JSON sidecar (not compact JSON). Records at 0.1 dBZ: 597,737 B zlib9 for 619,321 voxels, versus 2,060,602 B zlib9 for the prototype's JSON. 0.5 dB storage is 12.5% smaller but moves the >=35 dBZ count by 13 voxels (99,867 vs 99,854), so 0.1 dB is required for exact thresholds.
MESH footprint (roadmap item 4) is the same run and manifest: MESH_00.50 35,226 B gz per 2-min step (0.16% of the 33-level input). Its GeoJSON size is not measured.
numbers: MRMS gz per 2-min step, 33 levels: 18,435,716 B (2026-10-17 03:04:41Z, measured) to 29,444,582 B (2025-06-15 23:12:41Z, measured); 2-h mean 21,347,857 B (mrms.json). 11 levels: 6,424,019 to 10,509,537 B (measured).
GOES per 5-min step: G19 ACHAC 316,623 B + band 13 3,909,220 B = 4.23 MB (goes-aws listing, 01:41 scan); G18 pair about 4.0 MB.
Voxels at >=20 / >=35 / >=50 dBZ, 33 levels, event frame 23:12:41Z: 619,321 / 99,854 / 13,482 (exact match to the prototype JSON). Quiet frame 03:04:41Z: 0 voxels.

Event frame zlib9: 0.1 dB row-delta >=20 = 597,737 B (raw 2,524,056 B); 0.5 dB row-delta >=20 = 523,217 B; dense 1-byte grid = 1,798,719 B; mask keyframe (1 byte per cell, 3 classes) = 238,142 B; 2-bit packed mask = 252,681 B.

Mask change between consecutive steps: event 23:12:41 to 23:14:39, 264,659 cells (0.966%), changed-cell list zlib9 133,853 B; quiet 03:04:41 to 03:06:38, 0 changed cells, 8 B. Keyframe every 10 frames.
Per-frame product (>=20 dBZ, 0.1 dB): active delta 731,590 B; peak keyframe 835,879 B; quiet keyframe 104,214 B (averages 10,421 B per frame over 10 frames).
GOES product per 5-min frame: band-13 Montana-box 8-bit crop 29,901 B zlib9 (44,239 in-box cells, 213.3-284.8 K) + ACHA 10 km crop 1,984 B = 31,885 B (scan 03:21:17Z, measured on cached files).

Monthly per crew machine (30 days; 8.5 storm days x 12 h = 3,060 MRMS + 1,224 GOES frames; 8.5 days is from the supervisor log, 26 of 92 summer-2025 days): A 70.5 GB central (61.6-95.3 GB); A with 11 levels 24.8-37.3 GB. B 0.42-1.82 GB (quiet to peak keyframes). C 0.13 / 3.53 / 4.48 GB (quiet / active / peak keyframes). D 0.07 / 2.28 / 2.60 GB.

Server 24/7 ingest, 30-day month: 33 levels 497.6 GB (MRMS 461.2 + GOES 36.5); 11 levels 175-264 GB; 4 levels (0.5, 3, 6, 10 km) 91 GB. Fleet outbound (10 machines, assumed): D 22.8 GB, C 35.3 GB. DigitalOcean's 500 GiB = 536.9 GB, so D's total of 520 GB is 97% of it if inbound counts.

Cost per month (USD): A $0 server (NOAA reads paid by the bucket owner by default; crew data cost unpriced). designs.name: Design A: Jinja-generated CesiumJS page inside the Flask app (/globe)
designs.one_paragraph: Design A serves /globe from the existing Flask app: a Jinja page embeds CesiumJS 1.146.0 from cdnjs with sha384 integrity (both hashes re-computed today against the live files) and a 15-item hand-written JavaScript file that draws and handles browser-only events. Python (a new globe.py) owns every number, time, freshness state, alert outline/marker/can't-tell choice and storm-cell decision; the prototype's JavaScript decisions (dBZ thresholds, marker-or-outline choice, toggle enabling) move to Python. No pip package and no installer change. The 50 MiB cap applies to the whole-repo zipball: about 0.96 MB after the change (1.83%, computed from the reproduced 914,145 B main zipball plus 47 KB estimated deflated). Every route sits behind a default-off setting, and the self-test checks only HTTP status, so the design adds explicit socket, content and gate tests. Cloud-top height (ACHAC 10 km, DQF 0 only) and 3D storms (MRMS, default >=35 dBZ, below-ground cells dropped, -99/-999 shown only as no radar data) are later gated phases. Main costs: a CDN dependency in the desktop shell with no offline 3D view, WebGL 2 unverified on WebView2 and WKWebView, and voxel payload size (about 9.4 MB per JSON frame at >=20 dBZ at the 2025-06-15 event step, computed from prototype-mrms.json).
js_duties: JS-1 fetch the JSON Python serves from /api/globe/* - only the page can fetch for the page; no transformation
JS-2 create the Cesium viewer (ion off, no picker or geocoder, ellipsoid terrain) and set the first view to the box Python sends - the WebGL context and camera exist only in the page
JS-3 add imagery layers from Python's URL templates, bounds and max zoom - Cesium fetches and draws tiles in the browser
JS-4 show or hide a layer when its checkbox changes - DOM click event
JS-5 add Python's outline GeoJSON as polylines and Python's marker points as points - vector drawing happens in WebGL
JS-6 show a place name while the pointer is over its point - pointer movement and picking exist only in the page
JS-7 create one point per storm cell from Python's position arrays and class index - WebGL point primitives
JS-8 on an exaggeration radio change, pick Python's height array for that factor and rebuild the points - click event; heights come from Python
JS-9 scale points by camera distance using Python's radius - camera state is browser-side
JS-10 fly the camera to Python's bounding sphere on the zoom button - camera control
JS-11 if the Cesium global is missing or the viewer will not start (no WebGL 2), show Python's 'could not load' text - only the page knows whether the library and WebGL started
JS-12 count imagery tile error events per layer and show the count - tile requests happen in the browser; Python state does not change
JS-13 re-fetch the JSON every 60 s (cadence from Python) and redraw only layers whose data changed - timers exist only in the page; staleness stays in Python
JS-14 publish window.globeProbe for the browser checks - browser-side facts; nothing on the server reads it
JS-15 CONDITIONAL, owner ruling: decode Python's packed binary storm frame into typed arrays - WebGL needs typed arrays; the byte layout is Python's (only if the JSON budget fails)
pip_packages_added: none for the app (standard library and the already-installed Flask only). Publish job only, outside the payload and installer: numpy, eccodes, netCDF4, pyproj. Installer consequence: none for design A; a GRIB2 or netCDF reader inside the app would need a new installer under AGENTS rule 2 (launcher.py:47-54 lists what is bundled).
designs.offline_and_selftest_behaviour: Self-test (NETWORK False, TESTING True) GETs /globe and /api/globe/layers (added to manifest selftest) and fails only on HTTP status 400 or more (updater.py:140-143); phase-1 target 30 s, worker timeout 90 s (updater.py:122); zero socket connects asserted by a patched socket.create_connection test. Per-layer states: in the self-test or with NETWORK False every live layer is Off ('Live feeds are off', weather.py:517-518); base maps show 'Not timed' with no state. With feeds reachable: Live with valid time, retrieved time and age. A failed refresh after good data: Stale, showing last good data with its age (serve.py layer_state rule). A failed refresh with no good data: Unavailable with the reason. '3D view could not load' is a separate status, not a layer state: it appears when cdnjs is blocked or offline, the SRI hash fails, or WebGL 2 is missing (including the MSHTML fallback on Windows without WebView2, webgl-runtime.json); the layer panel keeps working on Python states. Setting off: /globe returns 200 with the off page and /api/globe/* return 200 {enabled: false} without fetching anything.
phases: Phase 0: research scaffold and prototype outside the app (done). Done when: prototype browser checks pass (canvas nonblack 0.9943 > 0.2; toggle change 0.8846 > 0.02, prototype-globe.json) and the owner rules on the 15 JS duties and D-G1. Stop: no app change.

Phase 1: /globe 2D with base maps, USGS imagery, GOES GeoColor via GIBS, NWS radar image, NWS alerts with null-geometry rules, places and territories; setting off by default; freshness on every layer; CSP; uncorrected parallax legend. Prerequisite: always-visible freshness on the flat map as its own small PR (live.html:218; maps.py:240). Done when: unittest discover 0 failures with at least 30 new globe tests; selftest PASS with NETWORK False in 30 s or less, /globe and /api/globe/layers listed; 0 socket connects; dev browser check: canvas nonblack > 0.2, a toggle changes more than 2% of canvas pixels, CDN-blocked run shows 'could not load' and 7 panel rows; alert parity 0 differences from alert_targets on at least 20 fixtures; 390 px width with bodyScrollWidth 390; zipball growth at most 50 KB deflated (estimate 47 KB). Stop: remove the nav tab and keep /globe behind the setting, or revert the merge.

Phase 2: cloud-top height from ACHAC 10 km, DQF 0 only; parallax legend first in the uncorrected wording, then the corrected wording. Done when: height product lag p95 at most 6 min after scan end over 7 days (scan-to-S3 max 125.3 s, goes-aws.json); 0 cells with DQF other than 0 drawn; legend equals parallax.json wording for the phase; one recorded high-top case shows higher than a low stratus case (owner picks the case). Stop: if the band-13 disagreement stays unexplained (r -0.66 CONUS, -0.62 Montana, goes-aws.json) or banner rights are unresolved, stay at phase 1.

Phase 3: 3D storms from the job's Montana box cut (default >=35 dBZ; >=20 dBZ only in a packed format). Done when: evaluation-predeclared.json metrics voxel_dbz_mismatch, no_data_rendered_as_echo_or_clear, threshold_count_parity and crop_and_level_integrity are 0 across the held-out cases; a frame is at most 2 MB transferred at the event step for >=35 dBZ (computed 1.52 MB raw JSON). Stop: any frame over 2 MB, or any no-data code drawn as echo: stay at phase 2.

Phase 4: time, with a 2-hour loop, scrub, per-frame valid time, and gaps shown as gaps. Done when: a 60-frame loop transfers at most 120 MB (computed 60 x 2 MB); missing_slot_shown_as_gap has 0 mismatches; frame count equals source count (no interpolated frames). Stop: keep the last frame with its age label.

Phase 5: laptop performance and outage behaviour. Done when: 30 fps measured on the owner's D-G7 laptop; browser memory under 1 GB; a frozen-clock outage test shows Live, then Stale, then Unavailable at the stated limits. Stop: keep phases 1 and 2 only.
biggest_risks: 1. Rule 4 creep: the prototype globe.js holds dBZ thresholds, alert marker/outline logic and toggle logic (globe.js:64-68, 224-232, 304-327). Control: the 15-item list is the contract; a test greps globe.js for threshold literals.

2. CDN and WebGL in the desktop shell: pinned and hash-checked but not offline; WebGL 2 is unverified on WebView2 and WKWebView; a Windows machine without WebView2 falls back to MSHTML, which has no WebGL 2 (webgl-runtime.json backend_table, F3 corrected).

3. MSL heights over flat ground: Billings ground is 952 m (terrain.json), so the 0.5 km MRMS level is about 450 m under the ground there. Control: below-ground filter; no terrain grid means no drawing. The statewide share is unverified.
4. Voxel payload: about 9.44 MB per JSON frame at >=20 dBZ, event step (computed); default >=35 dBZ; packed format only through JS-15.

5. Data rights: GOES files say 'Access is restricted to approved users only' while the registry says open (goes-aws.json); attribution needed (NOAA, NASA, USGS); EOX Sentinel-2 cloudless is non-commercial (base-imagery.json); Google 3D Tiles excluded (globe-libs.json).

6. Publish-job hosting: GitHub Actions terms limit use to developing and testing (hosting-options.json gh-terms-1, -2); a 1 GB Pages site holds 3.5-6.9 days of 2 MB products; object storage or a server is needed.
7. Freshness: D12 has one limit, and Feed.judge gives unknown keys 3600 s silently (weather.py:232). Control: CONTRACTS and FRESH_SECONDS entries, plus a failing test for a missing key.
8. CORS: ACAO * was seen on sampled objects only (gibs.json, goes-aws.json; one GIBS and one USGS tile re-checked today). A host without it fails silently; JS-12 is the only signal.
9. -99 and -999 are unverified (mrms.json; NSSL table unreadable): a misreading would turn no data into an all-clear. Control: 'no radar data' wording only.
10. Parallax: uncorrected cloud tops sit about 3-4 km off for a 2 km top and 20-33 km off for 12-15 km tops (parallax.json; its self-test re-run today, 9/9).
11. No browser step in CI (check-app.yml runs the self-test and unittest only), so JS regressions can pass CI. Control: dev browser check and owner sign-off per phase.
12. Cesium's bundled default ion token and whether ion-off makes zero requests are untraced (globe-libs.json open question).
13. Library churn: VoxelPrimitive is experimental; @cesium/engine exports are deprecated and removed in 1.150 (globe-libs.json; CHANGES 1.146). Control: exact pin and hashes only, no version ranges.

designs.name: Design B: separate globe window served by the desktop shell, outside the payload
designs.one_paragraph: Design B runs the globe as a second private server inside the desktop shell (desktop/globe/): waitress on 127.0.0.1 with a random port, a per-launch key, a Host check and its own cookie hw_globe, following the D2 gate. It reads the shared SQLite file read-only and takes its alert matches, places and frame metadata from an append-only snapshot table that the payload writes. The library (default CesiumJS 1.146.0, Apache-2.0) is pinned in desktop/globe/libs.lock.json with a sha384 per file, fetched by build.py at build time, checked again at startup, never committed, served without a CDN and with no ion token. Decoding runs in a child process: netCDF4 for GOES, and a statewide MRMS product for volumes, because continuous raw decoding on each machine would move 64.6 GB (GOES) and 432.3 GB (MRMS, 33 levels) per machine-month (computed). Installer cost: about 35.0 MB of Windows wheels for netCDF4 and numpy plus 2.1 to 13.1 MB of library files, with one installer per OS per globe change; the zipball grows only by about 67 KB of compressed code (computed), and the current HEAD zipball is 5.63% of the 52,428,800 B cap. Blocker: the desktop app is parked by D27 (DECISIONS.md:314-323), so owner decision O1 comes first. Corrections recorded: W12's claim that eccodes has no Windows wheel is wrong for 2.50.0 (the wheel contains ecCodes DLLs; decoding is untested there), and pygrib has no Windows wheel. Thirteen hand-written JavaScript duties (G-JS1 to G-JS13) are listed for owner ruling; eleven owner decisions are in the JSON file.
js_duties: G-JS1: probe WebGL2; if absent show '3D view could not load' (only the page can ask its browser for a WebGL2 context).
G-JS2: catch library script load errors and show the same banner (script load and error events exist only in the page).
G-JS3: create the viewer from Python-supplied options: no ion token, base picker and geocoder off, ellipsoid terrain (viewer objects exist only in the page).
G-JS4: request /globe/api/state at load and at the interval Python sends (the page must make the request; no time arithmetic in JS).
G-JS5: on a failed request show the server's last text with 'could not refresh', never an all-clear (only the page knows its request failed).
G-JS6: add, remove and reorder imagery and data sources from Python's tile URLs and GeoJSON (tile fetches and GPU upload happen only in the page).
G-JS7: show or hide a layer on checkbox change (input events exist only in the page).
G-JS8: select a frame index from Python's frame list on slider input, never interpolating (input events exist only in the page).
G-JS9: on hover or tap show Python-written text for the picked feature (pointer events and the library's pick exist only in the page).
G-JS10: count tile load failures per layer and print the count; state still comes from Python (tile load events exist only in the page).
G-JS11: size voxel points from camera distance using Python's constants; rendering only, owner ruling needed (the camera exists only in the page).
G-JS12: pause polling and drawing while the window is hidden, and resize the canvas (visibility and resize events exist only in the page).
G-JS13: phase 4 only; step through Python's frame list on a timer for playback (timers exist only in the page; frames are never interpolated).

numpy==2.5.4 for array code (C2); Windows cp312 wheel 12,573,091 B; macOS arm64 cp312 wheel 12,015,718 B (checked live)

designs.offline_and_selftest_behaviour: Self-test (python desktop/launcher.py --selftest globe, network off, 90 s limit as updater.py:122): every feed shows Off, and the base map shows 'no time' with tile status rather than Live. Checks: sha384 of every bundled file equals libs.lock.json; GET /globe is 403 without the cookie and 200 with it, showing 'Off' and 'Data unavailable'; the database opens read-only; no outbound socket. Live with the network down: alerts keep the last verified list with its age (Stale), or 'Alerts not checked' if never verified. Proposed limits: NWS radar Stale after 15 min (D12) and Unavailable after 60 min; MRMS volume Stale after 10 min since valid time and Unavailable after 30 min; GOES ACHA from AWS Stale after 20 min and Unavailable after 60 min; GOES drape via GIBS Stale after 60 min and Unavailable after 3 h. Nothing ever shows an all-clear. '3D view could not load' is a separate banner (WebGL2 absent, script error, sha384 mismatch) and the layer panel keeps working. Setting off returns 404 and hides the payload link. Details: design-b.json offline_and_selftest and freshness_and_kinds.
phases: Phase 0, decisions and feasibility (no product code): O1 recorded in DECISIONS naming D27; WebGL2 context on 2 of 2 crew-class machines (Windows WebView2, macOS WKWebView); eccodes 2.50.0 Windows decode count equals the Linux count (difference 0); 10-minute writer and reader test with 0 lock errors and p95 commit latency recorded. Stop: O1 refused closes design B; no WebGL2 on crew hardware means 2D map only.

Stop: any duty beyond G-JS1 to G-JS13 without owner ruling, or canvas share below 0.90.

Phase 2, cloud-top height (ACHA, satellite estimate) with parallax disclosed: acha_height_error 0 mismatched valid pixels on 3 recorded scenes; acha_geolocation_error p95 at most 2.0 km, or the exact uncorrected wording from parallax.json; acha_time_and_satellite 0 mismatches. Stop: any height mismatch means drape only.

Phase 3, 3D storm volumes (MRMS): zero mismatches on voxel_dbz_mismatch, no_data_rendered_as_echo_or_clear, threshold_count_parity and crop_and_level_integrity; replays of hail days 2025-06-13, 06-20 and 07-28, quiet days 06-03 and 08-02, night case 07-21, and the 06-20 radar-gap point 324.8 km from KGGW; frame_time_error 0 s; at most 1.0 MB per frame and 60 MB per 2-hour loop (proposed budgets). Stop: any fidelity metric above zero means 3D storms off.
Phase 4, time loop: valid-time error 0 s over a 2-hour replay; missing_slot_shown_as_gap = 1.0; zero interpolated frames. Stop: any interpolated frame means snapshot frames only.

2. WebGL2 on Windows is unknown: WebView2 WebGL2 is not stated; without WebView2 pywebview uses MSHTML (no WebGL2) with no browser fallback (winforms.py:94, 147-155); WebView2 runtime is over 250 MB.

4. Installer churn and manual delivery: one installer per OS per shell change (build.py:4); crews download by hand; no automatic shell update (D3).
5. Shared SQLite: no journal_mode is set (store.py:79-82, timeout 10 s); reader locks can stall the payload writer; WAL behaviour unverified (sqlite.org returned 503 twice).
6. Second server surface: the prototype server has no session key or Host check (serve.py); design B copies the D2 gate with its own cookie (RFC 6265 section 8.5, verified quote).

7. Library and licence: Viewer defaults call ion (globe-libs.json facts 31-32); VoxelPrimitive and deck.gl GlobeView are experimental (facts 35, 42); a custom volume shader adds hand-written JavaScript (rule 4).

9. Data terms: GOES files carry 'Access is restricted to approved users only' while the registry says open (goes-aws.json); wording needs counsel.
10. Test gap: CI has no browser step (check-app.yml:22-26); the prototype browser suite takes 127 s.
11. Hardware: RAM and GPU floor undecided (D-G7); the decode worker peaks at 409 MB (prototype-mrms.json).

designs.name: Design C: Python-first 2.5D on the flat map, no globe library; pydeck/MapLibre globe as a gated later phase
designs.one_paragraph: Recommended first build is C2, with no globe library. Python builds fixed-region PNG echo-top and cloud-top class layers, and fixed-transect SVG profiles. Inputs are MRMS MergedReflectivityQC (11 of 33 MSL levels, with below-ground levels masked by a Python-built terrain grid), GOES ACHA cloud-top height, and a GOES Band 13 picture. Producers are website/gridded.py plus a new website/volume.py, or payload/globe.py if the parked app resumes. The browser shows them on the vendored Leaflet 1.9.4 map (sha256 matches npm) with 6 new duties, 13 in total with the existing 7. C1 (pydeck 0.9.3 to a MapLibre globe with deck.gl 9.4.0) is a gated Phase 5 owner decision. pydeck has no GlobeView class (only map_projection='globe' on MapLibre). deck.gl 9.4.0 has no VolumeLayer (0 matches), and GlobeView is marked experimental. pydeck's HTML loads third-party scripts and stylesheets even with offline=True, and the app would need numpy, which means a new installer under rule 2. Neither option renders true 3D storm volumes, so the owner's 3D wish is met only in part. Since D27 the product is a website; the self-test, 50 MiB zipball and installer constraints describe the parked app, and the design says what carries over.

biggest_risks: 1. JavaScript scope creep against rule 4 and roadmap Next 9: C1 adds 8 hand-written duties, one of them GLSL, to a map.js that is already 2,155 lines. Mitigation: C2 first, with owner sign-off per C1 duty.

2. Parallax over-reading: uncorrected cloud tops sit about 3-4 km off for a 2 km top and 20-33 km off for a 12-15 km top (parallax.json), and a 3D look invites 'holographic' expectations. Mitigation: verbatim legend; no fly-to.
3. Cloud-top validity: no ground truth, and Montana valid cells correlate r = -0.62 with Band 13 brightness temperature (goes-aws.json). Mitigation: 'estimated' label and the acha metrics.

4. Below-ground levels: 0.5 km is 452 m below ground at Billings (terrain.json); 1.0 km sits inside the 50 m margin. A wrong mask mislabels heights. Mitigation: margin mask; unmasked echo is never drawn.
5. MRMS -99 and -999 meanings are unverified (mrms.json). Mitigation: both read 'No radar data'; NSSL table check in P0.

6. Licence and terms: GOES files say 'Access is restricted to approved users only' while NODD says open (goes-aws.json); Actions terms say develop and test (gh-terms-1, -3). Mitigation: counsel reading before P1.
7. Schedule reliability: 5-minute floor, delays, possible drops and the 60-day disable (gh-sched-1, -2, -4, -6). Mitigation: next_expected_utc timestamps and a 25-minute page-age warning.
8. Phone and cellular cost is unmeasured: C1 loops run 14-100 MB per 2 h (rendering-options.json), and there is no device test (SwiftShader only).
9. App path: numpy and eccodes (62.16 MB Linux wheels, no Windows eccodes wheel), and WebView2 WebGL2 is unverified (webgl-runtime.json). C2 avoids all three.

judges.lens: Engineering cost and risk (slug judge-engineering): installer and SHELL_API impact (AGENTS rule 2, D3); whole-repo zipball against the 50 MiB cap; offline self-test; WebGL availability on WebView2, WKWebView, Linux and phones; CDN dependence and integrity; update path to crews; maintenance burden; performance plausibility; failure modes. The product is the static website (D27), so installer, SHELL_API, zipball and self-test criteria bind only the parked app; each design is scored on them where it touches them and on the website equivalent for the current host.

reasons: Current-host fit: a static Python build (website/build.py) published by Pages (website.yml), with no runtime server and no new library, which is what D27 chose ('no server to keep running', DECISIONS.md:353-354). The only library is vendored Leaflet 1.9.4; its sha256 db49d009... matches design C and the file on disk (147,552 B, checked).

Rule 4: the six new duties N1-N6 are DOM or browser-only (layer switch, transect choice, image error, age clock, ARIA), each needing the inline note AGENTS.md:66-72 already requires. Total duties would be 13. map.js is already 2,155 lines (114,696 B, checked) and ROADMAP Next 9 asks to shrink it; design C does not estimate the lines the new duties add.

Publishing risk is not new: the live site already publishes MRMS and HRRR frames through Actions and Pages (D28; about 45.7 MB downloaded per build per main-architecture.json, unreviewed). The GitHub terms sentence 'You may only access and use GitHub Actions to develop and test your application(s)' was quoted live (checked); the CDN example in gh-terms-3 (hosting-options.json, unreviewed) was cut off in my live fetch. The counsel question covers the whole site, not the globe increment.

Pages limits, checked live: 1 GB per site; 100 GB per month soft; a 10-minute deploy timeout (website.yml:165 uses 10). C2's 0.66 MB per visit (design budget, unmeasured) fits about 150,000 visits a month under the soft limit (computed).

Build cost: the job has a 15-minute limit (website.yml:38); the live build measured 32-51 s (main-architecture.json, unreviewed). Adding 11 MRMS levels costs about 6 s of decode (computed from 18.3 s per 33-level frame, pipeline-options.json, unreviewed) and 6.4 to 10.5 MB of download per build (design C). The 15-minute limit is not the binding constraint.

Real gap, new code needed: the rolling 7-frame echo window and the 12-frame loop cannot be built as written. load_previous fetches only data/state.json from the live site (build.py:472-478, checked) and gridded.py has no previous-frame fetch (grep, checked). Persistence needs a fetch of prior PNGs from the live site before deploy; if the live site is unreachable the window resets and shows as a gap. Medium cost.

Test gap: CI runs four site modules (website.yml:84); Playwright runs only for branch pushes (website.yml:99 and 96-105), so a map regression can reach main. Add a Chromium check for the new layers to the existing smoke pattern and run it before merge.

Failure surfacing is sound: a failed frame shows a per-layer gap (N4); a stale layer keeps its age (N5); a failed build does not deploy (the deploy job needs build and runs only when publish is true, website.yml:161-163), so the last good deployment stays up with the page-age banner after 25 minutes.

Owner items, not fatal: two new evidence kinds need a DECISIONS entry since D12 has none; the NOAA ACHA banner ('Access is restricted to approved users only', goes-aws.json) needs counsel; the cloud product is 10 km ACHAC with 41% valid cells, which is coarse; C2 does not give the owner's 3D view (outside this lens). C1 alone (MapLibre globe with deck.gl) scores about 4 here: WebGL2 is required, GlobeView is experimental, deck.gl has no VolumeLayer, and it needs numpy and a new installer if the app resumes (design-c.json; globe-libs.json, reviewed).

Budgets are partly unmeasured: the 60 KB echo-frame budget has a basis (clear-sky precipitation frames averaged 33.5 KB, main-architecture.json, unreviewed), but storm-day sizes are not measured. Design C's 'about 42 KB average frame' does not match the measured 2,696,906 B over 48 frames, which is 56 KB average (computed).
